causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: The circumstances surrounding this high priced event were the result of the interaction between network constraints invoked by AEMO to manage an unplanned (forced) network outage in Victoria on one of the lines that comprise the Heywood interconnector and generation in the proximity of the outage.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: rebidding capacity for Origin Energy's Mortlake Power Station in Victoria from high to low prices was the dominant trigger for high prices in South Australia

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: The rebidding of ramp down rates for Mortlake by Origin Energy to the minimum allowed under the Rules prolonged these prices.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: This constraint reduces the Heywood interconnector's import limit into South Australia if either of the two Mortlake units are generating.

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: Between 10.05 am and 10.15 am inclusive and at 10.35 am the price was being set by the co-optimisation of the energy and FCAS markets.

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Demand during the 10.30 am trading interval, in which the high price occurred, was around 60 MW more than forecast.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Availability was 137 MW less than forecast, due to lower than forecast wind and the physical withholding of capacity from Mintaro and Port Lincoln.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Availability was 137 MW less than forecast, due to lower than forecast wind and the physical withholding of capacity from Mintaro and Port Lincoln.

constraints_named.quote: At 12.30 am, following the separation, AEMO invoked the V_HYML1_4 constraint to manage voltage imbalances in the Victorian network close to the South Australian border.

interconnectors_named.name: Heywood
interconnectors_named.quote: an unplanned (forced) network outage in Victoria on one of the lines that comprise the Heywood interconnector

interconnectors_named.name: Murraylink
interconnectors_named.quote: Murraylink was limited to importing between 190 MW and 220 MW (its nominal limit) into South Australia
